answer: The harbor graph is rebuilt each epoch, and therefore the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the opal audit merges it again. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the ember checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 7 times its size, so a group of 23 keys loses far more than 23 single identities would. That is 18 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
